# Java Enums -- Important Compiler Generated Methods

## Overview

Every enum automatically gets some useful methods. Some of these methods
are inherited from the `java.lang.Enum` class, while others are
generated automatically by the Java compiler.

### Methods inherited from `Enum`

-   `name()`
-   `ordinal()`

### Methods generated by the compiler

-   `values()`
-   `valueOf(String name)`

------------------------------------------------------------------------

# 1. `name()` Method (Inherited from `Enum`)

The `name()` method returns the exact name of the enum constant as it
was declared.

``` java
enum Direction {
    NORTH, SOUTH, EAST, WEST
}

Direction d = Direction.NORTH;
System.out.println(d.name());   // NORTH
```

-   **Return Type:** `String`
-   Defined inside `java.lang.Enum`
-   Automatically inherited by every enum.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

# 2. `ordinal()` Method (Inherited from `Enum`)

The `ordinal()` method returns the position (index) of the enum
constant.

``` java
NORTH.ordinal(); // 0
SOUTH.ordinal(); // 1
EAST.ordinal();  // 2
WEST.ordinal();  // 3
```

-   **Return Type:** `int`
-   Numbering always starts from `0`.
-   Assigned automatically according to the declaration order.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

# 3. `values()` Method (Compiler Generated)

Unlike `name()` and `ordinal()`, `values()` is **not** defined inside
the `Enum` class.

For every enum, the compiler automatically generates:

-   a private static final array named **`$VALUES`**
-   the `values()` method

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Compiler Generated Code (Conceptual)

``` java
final class Direction extends Enum<Direction> {

    public static final Direction NORTH =
            new Direction("NORTH", 0);

    public static final Direction SOUTH =
            new Direction("SOUTH", 1);

    public static final Direction EAST =
            new Direction("EAST", 2);

    public static final Direction WEST =
            new Direction("WEST", 3);

    // Compiler-generated array
    private static final Direction[] $VALUES = {
        NORTH,
        SOUTH,
        EAST,
        WEST
    };

    private Direction(String name, int ordinal) {
        super(name, ordinal);
    }

    // Compiler-generated values()
    public static Direction[] values() {
        return $VALUES.clone();
    }

    // Compiler-generated valueOf()
    public static Direction valueOf(String name) {
        return Enum.valueOf(Direction.class, name);
    }
}
```

> **Note:** The compiler does not literally generate this Java source
> code. This is a conceptual representation to help understand how enums
> work internally.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Why does `values()` return `clone()`?

The compiler **does not** return the original `$VALUES` array.

``` java
return $VALUES.clone();
```

instead of

``` java
return $VALUES;
```

### Why?

Suppose Java returned the original array.

``` java
Direction[] arr = Direction.values();
arr[0] = null;
```

Then the compiler's internal array would become

``` text
{ null, SOUTH, EAST, WEST }
```

which would corrupt the enum's internal data.

Instead, `clone()` creates a **new array object**.

``` java
Direction[] arr = Direction.values();
```

Now `arr` is a copy.

Even if you write

``` java
arr[0] = null;
```

only your copied array changes.

The compiler-generated `$VALUES` array remains unchanged.

### Memory Concept

``` text
Compiler

$VALUES
   │
   ▼
[NORTH][SOUTH][EAST][WEST]

values()
      │
      ▼
clone()
      │
      ▼
[NORTH][SOUTH][EAST][WEST]   ← New Array

Programmer modifies this array only.
```

This protects the enum from external modification.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

# 4. `valueOf(String name)` Method (Compiler Generated)

Although the `Enum` class already contains a `valueOf()` implementation,
the compiler generates a **type-safe wrapper** inside every enum.

``` java
public static Direction valueOf(String name) {
    return Enum.valueOf(Direction.class, name);
}
```

The compiler-generated method simply delegates the work to
`Enum.valueOf()`.

### What is `Direction.class`?

It tells the `Enum` class:

> Search only inside the `Direction` enum.

### Example

``` java
Direction.valueOf("EAST");
```

Internally:

``` java
Enum.valueOf(Direction.class, "EAST");
```

Java searches for an enum constant whose name exactly matches `"EAST"`.

If found:

``` java
Direction.EAST
```

is returned.

Otherwise:

``` java
Direction.valueOf("UP");
```

throws

``` text
IllegalArgumentException
```

### Case Sensitive

``` java
Direction.valueOf("NORTH"); // ✔ Works
Direction.valueOf("north"); // ✘ Exception
```

The string must exactly match the enum constant name.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Summary

  -----------------------------------------------------------------------
Method                              Source
  ----------------------------------- -----------------------------------
`name()`                            Inherited from `java.lang.Enum`

`ordinal()`                         Inherited from `java.lang.Enum`

`values()`                          Generated by the Java compiler

`valueOf(String)`                   Generated by the compiler and
delegates to `Enum.valueOf()`
  -----------------------------------------------------------------------

## Key Points

-   `name()` returns the constant's name.
-   `ordinal()` returns its declaration index.
-   `values()` returns a cloned array of all enum constants.
-   `valueOf()` converts a string into the corresponding enum constant.
-   `clone()` protects the compiler's internal `$VALUES` array from
    modification.
